title: Retain the finite optical controller, loss and acquisition costs
statement: The supplied finite resource table and controller calibration are conditional model bounds. The N=64 attempt uses 2689 interaction windows with m=20, real source/data preparation and qualified holding. The optical budget0.02 example has conditional Bell-infidelity<=0.0179344 and mean source attempts<=4.8927 under the stated source/detector/balanced-loss assumptions. Optical calibration and finite-cap resources remain additional. At fixed nonzero per-cycle loss the unfiltered direct architecture has exponentially growing worst-case interrogations as requested infidelity shrinks; purification/filtering or error correction is a separate supplied and paid layer. Singular-value-only exchange, unqualified dark/idle branches, coherent reused drains, bit-only parity checks, sampled all-state qualification and scalar filters for unknown operator amplitudes remain failed shortcuts. No performance advantage over the stronger ordinary comparators is established.

requires: Qutrit levels 0,1,e, risky/safe optical modes, at most one photon and H_tap=I*H_M+(|e><1|b+h.c.)*G with 0<g_minus I<=G(t)<=g_plus I; finite-dimensional propagators; continuum limits need their own qualified convergence

The logical dark level and quiet/idle branches share the same memory propagator; positive integrated coupling windows, qualified optical rotations/routing and outgoing fresh vacuum drain modes are supplied
Bell attempts use actual fresh |++> preparations after failures; source preparation/reset, detection, earlier-output disconnection and full holding histories are paid and qualified
Full flagged instruments and joint effects are required, rather than correct parity probabilities or scalar-effect identities alone
